easter_eggs.source: The bronze finial called 'the singing Odin', from the workshop of the 750s, in the Vendel style (ru.wikipedia 'Старая Ладога'; dossier 2, 7). No such helmet was worn.

easter_eggs.text: The thin white coins in the dealer's bag have no face on them, only lines of writing nobody north of the great steppe can read. The oldest of them were struck fifty-five years before the game begins, and the youngest in the bag he buried went into the ground seven summers before it.
easter_eggs.source: The oldest dirham hoard of the town ends in 786; single coins struck in 738-739; the oldest dirhams of European Russia (ru.wikipedia 'Старая Ладога'; en.wikipedia 'Staraya Ladoga'; dossier 4)

easter_eggs.text: The grain in the sacks on the bank is not the wheat of the Rhine. Four parts in five are a tough old kind with the husk tight on the kernel, which has to be pounded before it is ground. The women here think the western kind is for people with weak teeth.
easter_eggs.source: The burned barn of the 700s: wheat, 80 per cent emmer and 20 per cent soft wheat (ru.wikipedia 'Старая Ладога'; dossier 2). The opinion is invented.

easter_eggs.text: In the big house, in the years of the stone fort, a child has scratched a ship on a strip of birch bark: a hull, a mast, a steering oar, lines for the stays. It is kept on a shelf with the tally sticks, and nobody knows whose child.
easter_eggs.source: A birch-bark roll with a ship drawn on it, from the early 900s layers of Varangian Street (ru.wikipedia 'Старая Ладога'; dossier 2, 7). That a child drew it is a guess (?); shown from 900.

easter_eggs.text: From about 923 the tallest mound is shown to strangers as the grave of a prince who was killed by a snake out of his horse's skull. The mound was old when that prince was born: the spear in it is a hundred years older than he was. Another grave of his is shown at Kiev, and each town is sure.
easter_eggs.source: Oleg's Grave: dug in 1820, a two-barbed spearhead of the 700s or early 800s; the name may be of the 20th century (Petrenko), so that it was shown under his name this early is the game's liberty (?); the Novgorod chronicle (6430 = 922) puts his mound at Ladoga and the Kiev chronicle at Kiev (ru.wikipedia 'Олегова могила (Ладога)'; dossier 7)

easter_eggs.text: The pilot swears that far up, where the river leaves the upper lake, it sometimes turns and runs backwards for days. Every skipper laughs. He is right.
easter_eggs.source: The Volkhov's upper course can reverse its flow (en.wikipedia 'Volkhov (river)'; Research/water_levels/baltic_east.md; dossier 7)

easter_eggs.text: High in the river face of the stone fort, as high as five men, is a square hole with a beam above it. It is not a window. Bales go in by it straight from a boat, and in a siege so does everything else.
easter_eggs.source: The loading hatch 7 m up the river wall of the stone fort of about 900 (ru.wikipedia 'Староладожская крепость'; dossier 2). Shown 900 to 997.

easter_eggs.text: In the years of the stone fort a few pots stand on the big house's shelf that shine like polished copper and are only clay. They were made in the land where the white silver is struck, and came up two rivers and round a dozen rapids without breaking. The host will not let you drink from one.
easter_eggs.source: Lustre pottery from Mesopotamia in the early 900s layers of Varangian Street (ru.wikipedia 'Старая Ладога'; dossier 2, 4)

easter_eggs.text: Under the largest mound on the far bank an old man lies in a timber chamber, sixty or seventy winters old, with his horse beside him laid north to south and harness of the Baltic kind. Some who saw him buried say he had been washed by a priest, somewhere far away, long ago. Nobody put a hammer in with him.
easter_eggs.source: Plakun Mound 11: a chamber grave of a man of 60 to 70 with a horse, perhaps a Christian; horses laid north to south with Baltic horse gear (ru.wikipedia 'Плакун (урочище)'; dossier 2, 6). Shown from the 900s.

easter_eggs.text: The posts on the bank have no name that a stranger is told. A Frisian who asks which god it is gets the answer: the one who brings buyers. Nobody at the post thinks this is a joke.
easter_eggs.source: invented, after Ibn Fadlan's Rus traders of 922 (in paraphrase: realms/rus.md scene 4). No temple or idol is recorded here (dossier 8).

easter_eggs.text: The woman who was given this town as a wedding present in 1019 never lived in it. Long after the game ends she is a saint of the Greek rite at Novgorod under another name, with two feast days, one of them the fourth day of October.
easter_eggs.source: Ingigerd, later honoured as St Anna of Novgorod, 10 February and 4 October (en.wikipedia 'Ingegerd Olofsdotter of Sweden'); the veneration is long after 1066 (?) (dossier 6)

unlocks.what: The count in skins and beads
unlocks.how: End 'A bead for a pelt' by walking the whole row yourself, or trade through Ihalempi on three separate calls.
unlocks.gives: Furs at the trappers' price on the trading bank (buy_at_source), and the knowledge of what a timber of each fur is against beads, cloth and iron (learn): nobody on this river shorts the house on a count again. Inherited at half, as feeling is.

unlocks.what: Writing silver, weighed out to you at the head of the road
unlocks.how: Sell anything to Vigmund before 816, or furs to any dealer here in a later age.
unlocks.gives: The thread's flag sv_first_dirham if the house does not hold it yet (flag sv_first_dirham). The moneyer at Dorestad and Holmfast at Birka each have something to say about it.

unlocks.what: Budimir's marks for the lake shore and the river
unlocks.how: Hire the pilot three times and come through without touching; he, and his sons after him, then show the marks for nothing.
unlocks.gives: Counts toward unlock_pilot_volkhov (unlocks_793.json): no pilot is needed between the lake and the rapids, and the south shore is no longer doubtful for this house (learn).

unlocks.what: The smith's riddle of the corpse on a corpse
unlocks.how: Have Audvald, or the smith after him, mend something on your boat, and wait for him to set it.
unlocks.gives: give_riddle r-gest-24 (riddles_793.json): answered, it leads to the small hoard at the mounds (rw_hoard_ladoga).

unlocks.what: A rune stick left for a week's ale
unlocks.how: From 871: lodge on the Northmen's street and ask the host what the skald left; from 881 Hallstein reads it to you himself.
unlocks.gives: give_riddle r-gest-15 (riddles_793.json), one step of the chain of Delling's door that begins and ends at Uppsalir (the spine's riddle_road).

unlocks.what: A stanza cut on a stick by a trader wintering on the river
unlocks.how: Winter here, or drink with a man who has, and ask what he did with the dark months.
unlocks.gives: give_text t-vafth-43 (texts_793.json: given by a trader at aldeigjuborg, 793 to 1066).

unlocks.what: A bench in the big house with the house's mark on it
unlocks.how: End 'Ash on the Volkhov' with a fair scale, or pay for the first roof on the burned bank.
unlocks.gives: From 881: lodge, ask_news and rent_store cost nothing on the Northmen's street, and the host holds a message or a chest for the house over any winter. Inherited at half.

unlocks.what: The peace of the princess's jarl
unlocks.how: End 'The black stone' by carrying the townspeople out or by trusting the fort, and come before Ragnvald between 1019 and 1030; or bring him true word of the western kings on three calls.
